families.name: SUPPORTED_PROVIDER_SESSIONS
families.coverage: Identical query text executes concurrently through independent production compilation sessions with distinct provider schemas and row values; no cross-session rows or schema bindings were observed.

families.name: PARAMETERS_AND_SOURCE_SETTINGS
families.coverage: Distinct runtime parameter snapshots and source-setting resolver values are exercised concurrently; parameter cases are frozen in the contract and settings are a supporting isolation control.

families.name: DIAGNOSTIC_LOCATIONS_AND_CORRELATIONS
families.coverage: Concurrent invalid queries retain their own candidate marker and source span, while compiler internal-error contexts receive unique internal correlation IDs and sanitized public messages.

families.name: QUERY_LOCAL_ENUM_DESCRIPTORS
families.coverage: Concurrent query-local enum metadata compilations retain distinct enum names and fingerprints without descriptor crossover.

families.name: HISTORICAL_STAR_MODIFIER_SESSIONS
families.coverage: The historical full-star modifier query executes concurrently with distinct projected values; exclusion, replacement and rename semantics remain session-local.

contract.verificationResult: 60/60 frozen cases verified before authoritative replay; no frozen expectation was replaced.

initialObservations.finding: The first calibration incorrectly expected Name to remain in the historical LIKE star projection even though that modifier excludes it; the failure was a fixture oracle issue, not a production finding.
A no-build replay ran stale binaries after the fixture correction; it is retained as calibration evidence and is not authoritative.
After correcting the oracle to assert a unique projected Money value and rebuilding the focused fixture, all four test methods passed.
The frozen REC-136 matrix and supporting concurrent settings, correlation and descriptor controls passed after manifest freeze against the Release binaries.

repairAttempts.note: No production repair was made; the test oracle was corrected to assert a discriminating projected value, then the focused binaries were rebuilt.

focusedReplay.coverage: The four MSTest methods execute all 60 frozen cases plus supporting source-setting, internal-correlation and query-local enum controls; all sessions use independent production runtime objects.

harnessContract.budget: 60 frozen cases; no credentials, external providers, live services, shell actors or AI calls; all values are synthetic fixture data.
harnessContract.supportedBoundary: The campaign qualifies concurrent independent production API sessions and does not infer that arbitrary mutable engine objects may be shared concurrently.
harnessContract.harnessBoundary: The permanent class is marked DoNotParallelize because the historical test base controls process/thread culture and shared test compilation coordination; the class itself creates independent production sessions concurrently.
harnessContract.acceptanceBoundary: The results establish supported engine-session diagnostic isolation only. They do not certify installed CLI behavior, host integration, product-wide concurrency, human workflow or AI-agent safety.

obligations.REC-136-O01: Supported production concurrency boundaries and test-harness global state were inventoried before selecting reusable objects.
obligations.REC-136-O02: Independent concurrent sessions with identical query text and distinct schemas, parameters and supporting settings completed without cross-session values.
obligations.REC-136-O03: Concurrent diagnostic locations, candidate markers, internal correlation IDs and query-local enum descriptors remained session-specific.
obligations.REC-136-O04: The historical non-parallel star fixture was replayed concurrently; its scheduler/culture restriction was classified as harness state, while production session isolation passed.
obligations.acceptance: The 60-case frozen matrix passed 4/4 MSTest methods, the adjacent evaluator controls passed 68/68, campaign-tool self-tests passed 46/46 and the eight-target Release gate passed.
